clue.text: Displays opera-hat, the one that brings the house down

definitions.text: the one that brings the house down

parts.note: to display something is to show it, so displays gives shows
an opera hat is a collapsible top hat, colloquially called a topper

explanation.surface: Someone shows off a collapsible top hat and wins thunderous applause from the theatre audience.
explanation.walkthrough: To bring the house down is to win huge applause in a theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: An act so popular that the applause halts the performance is the one that brings the house down.

explanation.surface: A railway whistle described as something funny.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoot is the blast of a horn or whistle, and also something or someone very funny.

explanation.surface: A laundry room set into a bay.
explanation.walkthrough: The Wash is a large square bay on the east coast of England, between Lincolnshire and Norfolk.
explanation.definitionFit: The weekly wash is the laundry to be cleaned; The Wash is also the name of an English coastal bay.

clue.text: Endeavour to embrace old people in such adversity

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold within, so one piece wraps round the other

parts.note: to endeavour is to try
the aged are old people

explanation.surface: An encouragement to make an effort to look after the elderly in hard times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to embrace' puts AGED inside TRY, splitting it TR...Y.
explanation.definitionFit: A tragedy is a disaster or calamity, which is what adversity amounts to.

parts.note: par is the standard or normal level
a T-square is a kind of square used in technical drawing

explanation.surface: A description of a regular kind of square segment.
explanation.definitionFit: A part is a portion or division of a whole, just as a section is.

indicators.note: possibly says the letters of the next word may be arranged in another way

explanation.surface: A guess that the closest thing is from the Orient.
explanation.definitionFit: Oriental and eastern both describe things from the countries of Asia.

clue.text: Wear ring in this high gallery?

parts.note: to wear clothes is to dress
a ring is a circle

explanation.surface: A suggestion to wear jewellery when sitting up in the theatre's balcony.
explanation.walkthrough: The dress circle is the first raised tier in a theatre, where evening dress was once expected.
explanation.definitionFit: The dress circle is a raised seating tier in a theatre, above the stalls.

clue.text: It could cover Gloucester and most of Colchester, he discovers

indicators.note: discovers suggests the letters are uncovered and laid out afresh in a new order
most of a word is all but its final letter, so the place name loses its end

explanation.surface: Someone finds a wrapping that would cover two English towns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' drops the last R of Colchester; 'discovers' rearranges COLCHESTE with HE. Gloucester here is the cheese (Double Gloucester), not the city.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose cotton fabric is traditionally wrapped round cheeses such as Gloucester while they mature.

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A bridge said to have an odd personality.
explanation.definitionFit: An arch is a curved span, and a bridge is often built as one.

parts.note: keep reads as a noun for confinement, a punishment served inside one's home rather than in prison

explanation.definitionFit: A legal confinement to one's own home is a way of keeping someone indoors.

indicators.note: about indicates the letters are turned around into a new order

explanation.surface: A man, say, is dishonest from time to time.
explanation.walkthrough: Man is the Isle of Man in the Irish Sea, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isle of Man is an island, and an isle is an island.

parts.note: the letter L said out loud matches the French word elle, meaning she, so it describes a female person from France

explanation.definitionFit: Elle is French for she, so a female citizen of France is an elle.

clue.text: As unfortunate as Romeo and Juliet in actors' dress that is loose

definitions.text: As unfortunate as Romeo and Juliet

indicators.note: loose says the letters are set free and rearranged

explanation.surface: The actors' costumes for a Shakespeare tragedy are baggy.
explanation.walkthrough: Shakespeare's prologue calls Romeo and Juliet a pair of ill-fated lovers in just this phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill-starred lovers doomed by fate, as the prologue to Shakespeare's play describes the pair.

clue.text: Building's large cask is in road-broken

indicators.note: is in says one piece sits inside another
broken says the letters of the word before are rearranged

parts.note: a tun is a large cask for wine or beer

explanation.surface: A big barrel lies in a damaged road outside a building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' turns ROAD into RODA, and 'is in' puts TUN inside it, between RO and DA. The definition reads 'Building is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotunda is a round building, typically domed.

clue.text: Writer whose hardback, though slow, was a winner

definitions.text: Writer whose hardback, though slow, was a winner

parts.words: Writer whose hardback, though slow, was a winner
parts.note: hardback reads not as a book but as a creature with a hard shell on its back, the tortoise that beat the hare in a famous fable

explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Greek fabulist wrote of the tortoise who won a race against a hare.

parts.note: in Alice's Adventures in Wonderland the Dormouse tells of three sisters living at the bottom of a well, and this asks what filled that well

explanation.walkthrough: 'Carrel's' must be Carroll's, as in Lewis Carroll; the Dormouse's three sisters lived in a well of sticky syrup.
explanation.definitionFit: In Lewis Carroll's story, the three little sisters lived at the bottom of a syrup well.

indicators.note: about says the first word goes around the next piece

explanation.surface: A dog's tail is pretty much correct.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads 'Dog is', where dog is a verb meaning follow. 'about' puts R inside TAIL.
explanation.definitionFit: To dog someone is to follow them closely, which is to trail them.

indicators.note: about says the story goes around the next piece

parts.note: a yarn is a story, often a tall one

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A lengthy tale concerning a ruler of Ethiopia.
explanation.definitionFit: To long for something is to desire it deeply.

parts.note: No, also spelt Noh, is classical Japanese masked drama
a jolly is old slang for a Royal Marine, abbreviated RM

explanation.surface: Japanese theatre is described as fairly ordinary.
explanation.definitionFit: The norm is the usual or standard level, the average.

clue.text: Morale has no limits in spoken exam

indicators.note: no limits means the word loses its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Confidence is boundless in a spoken test.
explanation.definitionFit: An oral is a test conducted by speaking rather than writing.

clue.text: Hood and sash worn in the navy

indicators.note: worn in says the garment piece sits inside the other

parts.note: RN is the Royal Navy
an obi is a Japanese sash worn with a kimono

explanation.surface: A hood and a sash are part of naval uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: Hood is the outlaw of Sherwood Forest, Robin Hood, not a head covering.
explanation.definitionFit: The English folk-hero outlaw is known by first name and surname together, so Hood calls up his first name.

clue.text: Petroleum for sailor on Gibraltar, for example

indicators.note: on says the sailor is placed alongside the place

parts.note: Gibraltar is known as the Rock
a tar is a sailor

explanation.surface: Fuel for a seaman stationed on Gibraltar.
explanation.definitionFit: Rock tar is an old name for crude mineral oil found in rocks.

clue.text: Indifferent car is not in gear

explanation.surface: An apathetic description of a car that is idling.
explanation.definitionFit: Neutral means impartial, taking no side; it is also the gearbox position engaging no gear.

clue.text: Kind of car difficult to cover?

parts.note: difficult means hard
a top is a cover or lid

explanation.surface: A question about a type of car that is hard to put a cover on.
explanation.definitionFit: A hardtop is a motor vehicle with a rigid roof.

parts.note: a lea is a meadow, in poetry

indicators.note: neglected suggests the word is left in disarray, its letters jumbled

explanation.surface: A stretch of grassland has been abandoned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'neglected' turns LEFT into FLET. Tract here is a pamphlet, not an area of land.
explanation.definitionFit: A tract is a short printed pamphlet, often religious or political.

clue.text: Top cut off joint in this oven?

indicators.note: with the top cut off, the word loses its first letter

parts.note: a roast is a joint of meat

explanation.surface: A joint of meat with its top trimmed in the oven.
explanation.definitionFit: An oast is a kiln for drying hops.

indicators.note: found in says the answer sits within the words that follow

explanation.surface: Powder is discovered in the cupboards of a hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: Talc is a soft mineral ground into a fine powder for the skin.

parts.note: p, for piano, is the musical marking for quiet
a lay is a ballad or narrative poem

explanation.surface: A gentle song to be performed.
explanation.definitionFit: To play is to perform music or a part on stage.

clue.text: … suspect it could be loud to listener

parts.note: f, for forte, is the musical marking for loud
the ear is the organ that listens

explanation.surface: Continuing the song: one worries it might be too noisy for the audience.
explanation.definitionFit: To fear something is likely is to suspect or be apprehensive that it is so.

parts.note: steam is a source of energy
a roller is a long heavy sea wave

explanation.surface: An ancient road builder caught in a surge of power.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy steam-powered vehicle flattened road surfaces in road building.

clue.text: Carrying cargo not left in port

indicators.note: not means the following piece is removed

parts.note: a ship carrying cargo is laden

explanation.surface: A ship with freight is not allowed to stay in harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Aden is a seaport in Yemen.

parts.note: jobbers and bonds suggest stock-market dealers in securities, but bonds are patterns of laying bricks in a wall

explanation.definitionFit: Builders who lay courses of bricks arrange them in patterns called bonds.
